📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-03-eda-consumer-amqp-stopped-publishing`
This is occurrence #20 in the last 7 days (10th-occurrence resurface; last posted 2026-07-11T11:20:00Z, ~22h18m ago, still within the 24h window).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Integrations` (`@integrations` / `#team-integrations`)
Playbook: Confirm sibling P1 monitors (296632224 event-ingest, 296636101 Kafka-produce) — if both OK, core EDA pipeline is healthy and this is the documented benign idle-gap pattern, not an outage. Escalate only on sustained sibling co-firing or account impact.

Source alerts (1 total, degraded cycle — no Slack MCP read path, synthetic from DD monitor scan):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/296632224 (fired 2026-07-12T09:38:24Z)

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/296632224 — "[EDA][API][P1] Event ingest stopped (no POST /events traffic)" (OK at scan time)
  • DD monitor (sibling, co-fired 37s later): https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/296636101
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet_core.request.hits&exp_scope=env%3Aprod%2Cservice%3Aeda_orchestrator_api&exp_agg=sum&start=1783847304&end=1783849141 — 1 nonzero point (16 hits) then empty through fire time
  • DD logs (0 errors): https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Aeda_orchestrator_api%20status%3Aerror%20env%3Aprod&from_ts=1783847304000&to_ts=1783849141000&live=false
  • This-window concentration: eda_orchestrator_api only (both P1 siblings co-fired within 37s, same family flap; consumer AMQP sibling 296641466 fired separately at 10:21:26Z, see docs/investigations/2026-07-12-5a96b7412aa8b823.md)

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap`

Playbook: This is a new(ish) team:crm AMQP-consumer heartbeat/throughput monitor family that intermittently trips on genuinely-healthy bursty/low-volume traffic and self-recovers within minutes. Confirm the fired service's trace.amqp.command.hits shows near-threshold-but-present activity, and 0 error logs, before treating as actionable.

  • DD logs (0 errors): https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Amethod-mobile-notifications-subscriber%20status%3Aerror%20env%3Aprod&from_ts=1783852581000&to_ts=1783853781000&live=false

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-06-runtime-core-redis-cache-timeout-transient-burst`
This is occurrence #9 in the last 7 days (24h suppression window expired — last posted 2026-07-10T19:09:29Z, ~34h39m ago).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Vertical App Experience` (`@vertical-app-experience` / `#team-vertical-app-experience`)
Playbook: Confirm shape — check ES for `messageTemplate.keyword:"Redis operation timed out after 5 seconds"` and trace.redis.command.errors by service. If both are quiet (as this occurrence was), treat as an unconfirmed latency blip, not a repeat of the documented Redis-error spike.

Source alerts (2 total this batch, degraded cycle — no Slack MCP read path, synthetic from DD monitor scan):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/299544648 (fired 2026-07-12T05:48:48Z, gateway P95)
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/299551507 (fired 2026-07-12T05:49:07Z, ms-account-api P95, 19s later)

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/299544648 — "[Admin][Gateway][P2] P95 latency high (gateway)" (OK at scan time)
  • DD metric (Redis errors — sparse, below threshold): https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.redis.command.errors&exp_scope=env%3Aprod&exp_agg=sum&start=1783833528&end=1783842285
  • ES / Kibana: 0 hits for the documented Redis-timeout error signature in the 05:18:48Z-05:49:07Z window — this occurrence does NOT corroborate the KBs founding diagnosis; flagging for the team, not asserting a Redis root cause this time
  • This-window concentration: n/a — no error-log hits to aggregate; see docs/investigations/2026-07-12-fabba3832e3a41a3.md for full detail

⚠️ Note: this is the 2nd of 2 fires in this family today (occurrence #10, ms-account-api P95, also posts separately as a 10th-occurrence resurface) — both lack the ES corroboration the KBs original diagnosis relied on. Recommend the team re-examine whether these latency-only monitors belong bundled with the Redis-error-driven KB entry.

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-05-29-methodsession-getaccountbysubdomain-nre`
This is occurrence #19 in the last 7 days (24h suppression window expired — last posted 2026-07-07T13:19:00Z, ~4 days 18h53m ago).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `unmapped` (owner not resolved in ownership.md; the KB entry itself says "route to the platform-ui/MethodUI backend owner")
Playbook: Confirm synthetic-only via ES `message:"JWT Retrieval Failed"` aggregated by UserAgent — historically 100% WindowsPowerShell probe traffic, 0 real browsers, no customer impact. Two independent fixes on file: (a) code — null-guard `MethodSessionService.GetAccountBySubdomain()`; (b) monitoring — fix the Centreon synthetic check to send a valid subdomain.

Source alerts (1 total, degraded cycle — no Slack MCP read path, synthetic from DD monitor scan):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/299551647 (fired 2026-07-12T08:12:27Z)

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/299551647 — "[Admin][PortalApps][P1] 5xx error rate elevated (methodportal.com/apps)" (OK at scan time)
  • DD metric (traffic volume): https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet.request.hits&exp_scope=env%3Aprod%2Cservice%3Amethodportal.com%2Fapps&exp_agg=sum&start=1783843347&end=1783843947 — sparse, 1-3 hits/bucket
  • DD logs (0 errors): https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Amethodportal.com%2Fapps%20status%3Aerror%20env%3Aprod&from_ts=1783843347000&to_ts=1783843947000&live=false
  • ES / Kibana (0 hits — this occurrence did NOT reproduce the exact "JWT Retrieval Failed" signature; not asserting the specific NRE, but the low-traffic/self-recovered shape matches the KBs broader no-real-impact conclusion): see docs/investigations/2026-07-12-c79b6b03955ff987.md for the full query

⚠️ Note: this entry has no `evidence_source`/`evidence_query` declared — recommend adding one (the ES JWT-Retrieval-Failed-by-UserAgent aggregate from its own playbook) so future cycles auto-verify per the standard procedure.

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-06-rainforest-merchant-details-503-serviceunavailable`
This is occurrence #4 in the last 7 days (24h suppression window expired — last posted 2026-07-10T17:07:26Z, ~1 day 15h19m ago).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Transactions` (`@transactions` / `#team-transactions`)
Playbook: this occurrence deviates from the documented signature — see the flag below.

Source alerts (1 total, degraded cycle — no Slack MCP read path, synthetic from DD monitor scan):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/295882732 (fired 2026-07-12T08:26:53Z, Warn state)

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/295882732 — "[Rainforest] Outbound API Error Rate (4xx+5xx) > 5%"
  • ES / Kibana (2 hits — data present, corroborates a real Rainforest error, but NOT the documented one): `${KIBANA_BASE_URL}/app/discover#/?_g=(time:(from:'2026-07-12T07:56:53Z',to:'2026-07-12T08:26:53Z'))&_a=(query:(language:kuery,query:'fields.dd_service.keyword:%22runtime-core-api%22%20AND%20message:*rainforest*'))`

⚠️ **Evidence mismatch — flagging for the team, not asserting the documented root cause:** this occurrences 2 ES hits are `System.InvalidOperationException: Rainforest API returned status code: BadRequest` from `RainforestProvider.CreatePaymentMethodPayinAsync` (a rejected payment-method-id), NOT the KBs documented `GetMerchantAsync`/503 signature. Single request, account `alocetsystem` (Methods own internal system account — likely internal/test traffic, not a real customer). The monitor-name-only match criterion is bundling a distinct Rainforest-outbound failure mode under this entrys stale diagnosis. Recommend tightening the match to the specific error signature, or watching for a 2nd occurrence of this BadRequest shape before creating a dedicated entry. Full detail: docs/investigations/2026-07-12-3fd10124bd0c9144.md

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 5)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: code  •  alerts in group: 1
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `unmapped`

Symptoms:
  - rest-api POST /api/{version}/tables/{table} returned 596 5xx errors in a 30-minute window (~18.9x the monitors >30 threshold)
  - 100% concentrated on this one resource; 0 error logs (APM-only signal, no ES/Serilog corroboration)
  - Self-recovered by scan time; this is a RECURRING pattern — this exact monitor has fired dozens of times over the past ~2 months without ever being converted into a KB entry or (as far as we can tell) a filed defect

Trace IDs: none captured (APM-only, no log-level detail)
Likely cause: unconfirmed — a specific rest-api tables endpoint intermittently 500s in bursts, self-recovers, leaves no log trace. No deploy correlation checked this cycle.
Suggested next action: file defect (recurring pattern, ~2 months of unaddressed fires — see new KB entry `ki-2026-07-12-rest-api-tables-endpoint-5xx-recurring-burst` for full history)
